paragraphs.text: Loose [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition) from 2023, picked from wild, uncultivated plants. Anhua is a mountain county on the Zi river in north-central Hunan. Its name is a protected origin in China, and the county is widely held to be the main home of [dark tea](dark:definition) and a starting point of the old tea routes to the north-west.

Every Anhua tea begins as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), a raw tea of large local leaf that is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried, traditionally over a pine fire. The pile is what makes it dark tea. Left in warmth and moisture, the leaf is slowly darkened by microbes and its own chemistry, and that change goes on after the tea is made.

At three years this tea is young. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and is said to improve, though no agreed count of years marks it as aged. It wants clean, dry, aired keeping, away from mould and other smells.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
